description: RAIN keeps the state view current across 165 counties on every refresh — care-gap concentration, broadband dead zones against telehealth capacity, and ED divergence by clinic — so program oversight starts from a live map, not a quarterly spreadsheet.

Separates counties that trail because need is extreme from counties that trail because reach is thin — a distinction only visible when clinic risk tiers, county vulnerability, rurality, and site capacity are rolled up together.

Benchmarks every county against its own public baselines — CDC PLACES, SVI, RUCC, shortage designations — with source and vintage on each figure, so outperformance and shortfall are both defensible in a CMS submission.

Assembles the need-reach-outcomes reporting package directly from the conversation — county and clinic tables, provenance, dataset vintages, the synthetic-data label on every page — and distributes it scope-safe, each director seeing their own clinic before the rollup.
